memory_candidates.content: When adopting an upstream module that declares scoped notation on typeclass projections in a parent namespace, a fork that binds the same symbols to concrete constructors in child namespaces hits Lean 'Ambiguous term' errors -- scoped notation from an enclosing namespace is active inside its children. The staging trap: the tree is red from the moment the upstream module enters the import closure until every collision is resolved, so a naive 'vendor first, then fix' plan has an unbounded red window. The fix is a three-move sequence: (1) vendor the upstream file ORPHANED, outside the barrel, so nothing imports it yet; (2) pre-land the compensating `X_def : Concrete.x .. = Projection.x .. := rfl` bridge lemmas in green, one module per phase, while the local notation is still present -- both sides of the rfl already exist, so this is legal before the switch; (3) confine the import, the duplicate-class deletions, the notation deletions, and the barrel regeneration to one declared atomic-batch phase. This shrinks the red window from the whole task to a single phase and leaves every other phase independently committable.
